audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for governing authorities, taxes, love fulfilling Law, wakefulness. Include caution against absolutizing empire obedience.

verses.restored: Let every soul/life be subject to higher authorities; for there is no authority except under the Divine, and those existing have been arranged under the Divine.

familiar.text: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.

modern.text: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

original.text: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω, οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ θεοῦ, αἱ δὲ ⸀οὖσαι ⸀ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν.

verses.restored: Therefore the one resisting the authority has opposed the arrangement of the Divine, and those opposing will receive judgment for themselves.

familiar.text: Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.

modern.text: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.

original.text: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν, οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται.

verses.restored: For rulers are not a fear to the good work but to the harmful. Do you wish not to fear authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it.

familiar.text: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:

modern.text: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.

original.text: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος ⸂τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ⸃ ἀλλὰ ⸂τῷ κακῷ⸃. θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν; τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς·

verses.restored: For it is servant of the Divine to you for the good. But if you do the harmful, fear; for it does not bear the sword without purpose, for it is servant of the Divine, an avenger into wrath to the one practicing harm.

familiar.text: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil.

modern.text: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

original.text: θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν. ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς, φοβοῦ· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ· θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν, ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.

verses.restored: Therefore it is necessary to be subject, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience.

familiar.text: Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.

modern.text: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.

original.text: διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι, οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν,

verses.restored: For because of this you also pay taxes, for they are public servants of the Divine, attending to this very thing.

familiar.text: For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God’s ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.

modern.text: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε, λειτουργοὶ γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες.

verses.restored: Give back to all what is owed: tax to whom tax, tribute to whom tribute, fear/reverence to whom fear/reverence, honor to whom honor.

familiar.text: Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.

modern.text: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due. Love Fulfills the Law (Leviticus 19:9–18)

original.text: ⸀ἀπόδοτε πᾶσι τὰς ὀφειλάς, τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον, τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος, τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον, τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν.

verses.restored: Owe nothing to anyone except to love one another; for the one loving the other has fulfilled Law.

familiar.text: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.

modern.text: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

original.text: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε, εἰ μὴ τὸ ⸂ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν⸃· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν.

verses.restored: For the commandments, You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not desire, and if there is any other commandment, are summed up in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

familiar.text: For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

modern.text: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

original.text: τὸ γάρ· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις, καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή, ἐν ⸂τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ⸃ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται, ⸂ἐν τῷ⸃· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

verses.restored: Love does not work harm to the neighbor; therefore love is fulfillment of Law.

familiar.text: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.

modern.text: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. The Day Is Near

original.text: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται· πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη.

verses.restored: And this, knowing the season, that it is already the hour for you to awaken from sleep; for now our salvation/healing is nearer than when we trusted.

familiar.text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.

modern.text: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

original.text: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι ὥρα ⸂ἤδη ὑμᾶς⸃ ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι, νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν.

verses.restored: The night advanced, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us put away the works of darkness, and let us put on the weapons of light.

familiar.text: The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.

modern.text: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

original.text: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν. ⸀ἀποβαλώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους, ⸂ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ⸃ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός.

verses.restored: Let us walk beautifully/properly as in the day, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in bedchambers and sensual excess, not in strife and jealousy.

familiar.text: Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.

modern.text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

original.text: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν, μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις, μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις, μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ,

verses.restored: But put on the Lord Jesus Messiah, and make no forethought for flesh into desires.

familiar.text: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.

modern.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας.

safety_note: Romans 13:1-7 should not be absolutized into obedience to unjust state violence. It follows Romans 12's non-retaliation ethic and is bounded by Paul's wider witness that Divine authority judges authorities too. The chapter's center moves into love fulfilling Law and wakeful light.
